topic: The Cosmic Symphony: Linking π, Primes, and the Complex Plane
target_audience: Advanced High School or Early University Students

sections.title: The Strange Encounter
lecture_lines: Geometry's foundation is the circle and the constant pi.
Prime numbers are the discrete atoms of arithmetic.
How do smooth circles relate to jagged prime numbers?
animations: Fade in a large circle with radius 'r' and the symbol \u03c0 (#FFD700) at the center.
Fade in a sequence of prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11... (#00FFFF) below the circle.
Draw a glowing arrow connecting the primes to \u03c0, with a large question mark (#FFFFFF) above the arrow.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The 2D World of Numbers
lecture_lines: We expand the number line into a two-dimensional plane.
Multiplying by i rotates numbers by ninety degrees.
This geometry lets the unit circle trace out pi.
animations: Draw a horizontal real axis from -3 to 3 with tick marks (#FFFFFF).
Animate a 90-degree rotation of a vector from the real axis to the vertical imaginary axis 'i' (#FF00FF).
Draw a Unit Circle (#FFFF00) centered at the origin on the complex plane.

sections.title: The Basel Problem: The First Bridge
lecture_lines: Summing the squares of all reciprocal integers reveals a pattern.
As terms stack, the total converges to a limit.
This infinite sum unexpectedly reaches a specific value.
Leonhard Euler proved it equals pi squared over six.
Circles and integers are now mathematically tied together.
animations: Write the sum 1/1\u00b2 + 1/2\u00b2 + 1/3\u00b2 +... in white (#FFFFFF) at the top.
Below it, draw horizontal segments of lengths 1, 1/4, 1/9, etc., stacked end-to-end to show convergence.
The segments approach a vertical dashed line representing the total sum limit (#00FF00).
Replace the sum expression with \u03c0\u00b2 / 6 in bright gold (#FFD700).
Surround the \u03c0 symbol with a small pulsating circle to emphasize the geometric link.

sections.title: The Euler Product: Primes Join the Party
lecture_lines: Euler bridged the gap between integers and prime numbers.
Every integer sum transforms into a product of primes.
This equality is known as the Euler Product formula.
It proves that primes govern the behavior of circles.
This connects prime distribution directly to the zeta function.
animations: Show the Zeta sum \u2211 1/n^s on the left (#FFFFFF) and the Euler Product \u220f 1/(1-p^-s) on the right (#00FFFF).
Animate the prime numbers (2, 3, 5...) moving from the product side into the sum side.
Draw a large equals sign between the sum and the product in a flashing yellow (#FFFF00).
Highlight the term \u03c0\u00b2/6 from the previous section to show it is a specific value of this function.
Transform the formulas into a single glowing 'Zeta' symbol (#FF4500).

sections.title: The Riemann Landscape: Finding Regularity
lecture_lines: Riemann extended this function into the complex plane.
He mapped the zeros where the function's value vanishes.
These zeros align perfectly along a single vertical line.
Their rhythm defines the distribution of all prime numbers.
This landscape reveals the secret symmetry of the primes.
animations: Set up a coordinate grid representing the complex plane (#333333).
Draw a vertical line (the Critical Line) at Re(s) = 1/2 in bright green (#00FF00).
Animate several red dots (zeros) (#FF0000) appearing one by one exactly on this green line.
Add an oscillating wave representing the 'music of primes' whose rhythm depends on these zeros.
Flash the entire Critical Line to emphasize its role in the regularity of prime distribution.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Universal Code
lecture_lines: Pi, rotation, and primes weave a single mathematical fabric.
This symmetry secures the encryption of our digital world.
Geometry and numbers dance in one cosmic symphony.
animations: Display the symbols \u03c0, i, and p (primes) rotating slowly around a central point (#FFFFFF).
Transform these symbols into a digital padlock icon (#00FF00) representing modern encryption.
Fade out everything except the text 'The Cosmic Symphony' in large, glowing letters (#FFD700).
